answer: A task-ladder gate blocks bulk fake identities: each newcomer climbs one ladder. A newcomer starts at the jetty dock. The first rung locks 10 credits in the sable ledger. Later rungs demand 20 then 40 credits, so one identity risks 70. Falcon auditors sample rungs; copied work burns the deposit and bars that ladder. The failure mode is ladder rental: one worker climbing for many accounts leaves identical timing and phrasing, so auditors burn the set. The k-th fake pays a fresh 70 credits, so 1,000 fakes cost 70,000, while an honest agent pays 70 once and keeps standing.
